definitions_considered.exact_text: the degree of agreement among repeated measurements, indicated by their spread or range
the closeness of a measured value to the true value of the quantity
the smallest change in a quantity that a measuring instrument can distinguish, usually set by its smallest scale division
an error that causes measurements to be consistently offset from the true value in the same direction
an unpredictable variation in repeated measurements that causes readings to scatter about the true value
